messages:
jia: Quick follow-up from today's RFC sync — we need to finalize the SM capability surface and ownership boundaries for kernel routing across A100 / H100 / L4. I sketched a minimal capability API and a fallback contract. Posting it here for comments.

matt: thanks for writing this up, jia. can you paste the API sketch inline? easier to iterate in-thread. :+1:

jia: sure — minimal idea: each device advertises capabilities as a bitset + semantic names. runtime asks `probe(device)` once per boot and caches. example: 

```
// capability keys (strings) -> values (bool | enum)
{
  "sm_supports_warp32_attention": true,
  "max_vector_width": 128,
  "supports_tensorcore_qk_attention": "h100_only",
  "prefers_block_layout": "row_major",
}
```

contract: kernel selector must only pick kernels whose required keys are satisfied; otherwise runtime falls back to safe reference kernel (slower, widely compatible).

sam: two quick notes: (1) the `probe` output must be stable across reboots unless a driver update occurs, otherwise rollout/telemetry becomes noisy. (2) we need versioning on capability keys — add `cap_schema_version`.

jia: agreed on versioning. added: `cap_schema_version: "v1"`. also propose we include a short `confidence` score for auto-probed heuristics so ops can override via device profile.

nora: how do we expose this to Dedicated customers? we can't probe private hw in customer VPCs. we should provide a `device_profile` override in deployment manifest. fallback rule: manifests trump probes.

alex: from runtime side, important tradeoff: too many capability axes => combinatorial kernel variants. I propose we keep the surface minimal: 1) warp attention style (warp32 vs warp16), 2) tensorcore path (none / a100-like / h100-only), 3) max_block_kv_size. anything else becomes a heuristic that maps to these buckets.

matt: +1 on bucketing. also we should separate "performance preference" from "correctness requirement". correctness flags (e.g., `requires_fp32_accum`) must be mandatory for kernel safety. perf prefs (e.g., `prefers_tensorcore`) are advisory for selector.

sam: rollout plan idea: feature-flag new kernel selector behind canary. when selecting kernel we emit telemetry: `{device_id, chosen_kernel, probe_flags, latency, correctness_checks_passed}`. use that to slowly enable by device family and region.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary build 2026.03.20-kerneroute-v0 pushed to staging-cluster-3 at 2026-03-20T14:22:10Z

nora: operationally we also need an emergency fallback route that can be toggled per-customer if we see regressions. Suggest adding `fallback_policy` in runtime config: `auto-rollback`, `hard-fail`, or `route-to-reference`.

jia: good call. propose final API snippet for docs and SDK mapping: 

```
capability = {
  "cap_schema_version": "v1",
  "features": {
    "warp_attention": "warp32",  // warp32 | warp16 | generic
    "tensorcore_attention": "a100|h100|none",
    "max_kv_block": 4096
  },
  "confidence": 0.9
}
// runtime.select_kernel(model, device_capability, perf_hints)
```

sam: small UX ask for SDKs: make the capability object pluggable when creating a runtime client so private deployments can pass explicit profiles.

alex: question about attention optimizations: for L4 we have limited tensorcore support — should we treat L4 as `tensorcore_attention: none` or create a `l4_approx` category? L4 can do some fused ops but not full h100 kernels.

matt: I'd rather keep `none` and expose a perf_hint `allow_approximate_fusions: true` — keeps kernel matrix small while letting ops opt into approx paths. we can add `l4_approx` later if we see enough benefit.

nora: regarding tests: we need a small battery that runs correctness nets for attention across seq lens [32,128,512,2048] and compares outputs to reference within tolerance; also perf microbench for each kernel path. add to nightly and canary.

jia: noted. we'll add evalsets and thresholds to the rollout checklist. also, who owns the capability key definitions? infra or eng-runtime?

alex: eng-runtime should own the schema but infra owns the probe implementation and test harness. agree?

matt: agreed. product/pm can own the customer-facing docs and manifest keys. write up ownership doc and I'll add to RFC as follow-up.

sam: action items: 1) jia to add versioned schema draft + examples (due EOD Tue). 2) infra to implement probe + override hook (infra: @nora). 3) eng-runtime to implement selector with perf/correctness separation (eng-runtime: @alex). 4) devex to add SDK pluggable profile (I'll loop in later).

jia: thanks — I'll post the schema PR in `github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/rfcs` and add test vectors.

nora: tagging infra lead for visibility: @maria-infra (FYI).

matt: small policy note: add telemetry opt-out for enterprise customers in Private. make sure probe data respects PII policies.

jia: noted — will include data minimization doc. ok let's reconvene after the PRs land. :rocket:

alex: one more thought — long-term we might want a capability discovery registry (catalog) so we can reason cross-cluster about which kernels to maintain. opening an issue for that.

matt: nice, thanks everyone.
